messages.text: The heat sinks on a supra, so far, and I was going to hook the psu, to a thor 2.
I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let me check the Thor P2's input spec before you wire anything up.
Searched the web · Hammer Thor P2 miner power supply 12V input watts
Searched the web · "Thor P2" bitcoin miner specifications power consumption
Read the hammer miner thor p2 page

Heat sinks on a Supra are fine, that is just paste and metal, no warranty issue as long as you do not raise the clocks.

The P. on the Thor P2 is the one to be careful with. Two things:

1. The T. P2 takes its power through an **XT60** connector, and it draws about 166 W. The L.350-12 is an open-frame unit with bare screw terminals, no XT60 and no cord, so you would have to wire both the mains side and an XT60 pigtail yourself, and get the polarity right. That is doable but it is not plug and play.

2. Before anything else: look at the label on the brick your Thor P2 came with and tell me the **output voltage** it prints (12V, 19V, 24V?). The 350 is a 12V supply. If the stock brick is not 12V, the LRS-350-12 does not go anywhere near that miner.

What does the Thor P2 brick say?
Thank you.

Anytime. If you check that label and it reads 12V, come back and I will walk you through the XT60 side safely. And if you would rather not wire it at all, the Thor P2's stock brick is already sized for it, so there is no need to change anything.

Happy mining.
It came with the same power cord as the Thor 2 has.

That cord is the AC side, the one from the wall into the supply. Both use a standard mains cord, so matching there does not tell us anything about the DC side, which is the part that reaches the miner.

What I need is the small print on the Thor P2's own brick, the line that starts with **OUTPUT**. It will read something like "OUTPUT: 12V ⎓ 15A". Just that voltage number.

Two reasons it matters:
1. If the Thor P2 is 12V, the LRS-350-12 matches on voltage and has plenty of headroom (29A against the roughly 14A the miner pulls).
2. Even then, the LRS-350-12 has bare screw terminals, no XT60. The miner only takes XT60, so a pigtail has to be made up with the polarity correct. Nothing on the LRS can be plugged into the Thor P2 as it comes.

Read me the OUTPUT line and I will tell you which way to go.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

I opened the photo. The label reads MODEL: GM-H250S12, Shenzhen Qilink, Switch power supply, OUTPUT: 12V 25A on 176-264VAC and 12V 20.8A on 100-176VAC.

So that is a 250W, 12V brick. Good news and a caveat:

1. **Voltage matches.** The T. P2 is a 12V machine, so the LRS-350-12 is the right voltage. No risk of cooking it the way 12V would have cooked the 602.
2. **You do not gain anything by swapping.** On a US 120V outlet your stock supply gives 12V at 20.8A, about 250W, and the miner pulls roughly 166W (14A). It already has about 40 percent headroom, and it comes with the XT60 lead fitted.
3. The L.350-12 has bare screw terminals, so to use it you would wire mains onto it yourself and solder an XT60 pigtail onto V+ and V-. More work, more risk, for headroom you are not short of.

My honest advice: leave the Thor P2 on its own brick and keep the LRS-350-12 for a project that actually needs an open-frame supply, or for running several small 12V boards off one unit.

If you do want to build the pigtail anyway, say so and I will give you the polarity and the terminal order step by step. Rule one either way: never touch those screw terminals with the mains cord plugged in.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Opened it. I can see two yellow connectors in your hand: the left one is the bigger XT60 style with a black moulded housing, and the right one is clearly stamped **XT30**, the smaller version. Behind them is the Mean Well LRS-350-12 in its blue case, and there do look to be red and black leads already made up on the left of the frame.

Important: XT30 and XT60 do not mate. Same yellow plastic, different size, and the XT30 is the smaller one.

So, two things:

1. Which of those two is on the **Thor P2** end, and which is on the **LRS-350-12** end? The T. P2 takes XT60.
2. Does the LRS-350-12 already have that red/black lead wired onto its screw terminals, or is it loose in the kit box?

Answer those two and I will tell you whether it plugs straight in or whether you need an XT30 to XT60 adapter.
Those are the 2 plugs it came with.

That makes sense then: the kit gives you two output leads so the same supply can feed different miners. The X.60 one is the Thor P2's size, the XT30 one is for smaller boards.

Next check, no tools needed and nothing plugged in: take the XT60 lead (the bigger one, left in your photo) and offer it up to the connector on the **Thor P2 itself**, the socket the stock brick's cable goes into. It should slide together snugly with no force. If it does, that is your lead.

Tell me if it mates, and also whether the far end of that lead is bare copper or has ring/fork terminals crimped on. That decides the next step on the Mean Well screw block.
Yes the bigger one is the 60

Good, that is your lead.

Before the wiring step, one thing I still need: the far end of that XT60 lead, is it bare copper strands or does it have crimped fork / ring terminals on it?

While you look, the layout on the LRS-350-12 terminal block, left to right as the label reads:

1. **L**, **N**, **⏚** (earth) on the AC side. That is live mains, treat it as such.
2. Then **-V, -V, +V, +V** on the DC side. The X.60 lead's **red** goes to a +V screw, **black** goes to a -V screw.
3. There is a small brass pot marked **V-ADJ** near the terminals. Leave it alone, it is set to 12.0V from the factory.

Two rules I will keep repeating: the mains cord stays unplugged the whole time you have a screwdriver on that block, and once it is wired the exposed terminals want a cover or a box, not an open frame sitting on a desk.

Bare copper or forks?
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Opened it. That is already wired, and from what I can see it is wired correctly.

Reading your photo right to left on the block: brown on **L**, blue on **N**, green/yellow on the **earth**, then two black wires in blue fork terminals on the two **-V** screws, and two red wires in red forks on the two **+V** screws. All on insulated fork terminals, screws down, no stray strands showing. That is the right layout, and it looks like both leads (the XT60 and the XT30) are landed on their own pair.

Two steps before the miner goes anywhere near it:

1. Plug the mains cord in with **nothing** connected to the XT60 yet. The fan should spin or at least the unit should sit quiet with no buzz or smell. If you have a multimeter, probe inside the XT60 socket: you want about 12.0 to 12.3V, and the pin fed by the red wire must read positive. If it reads negative, the pair is swapped.
2. Unplug the mains again, then connect the Thor P2's XT60, then plug the mains back in. Never hot-plug the XT60, the inrush arcs the contacts.

One last thing and I will stop nagging: that terminal block is live mains at 120V and it is wide open. It needs the clear terminal cover or a box over it before it lives anywhere a hand or a cat can reach.

Does it come up to 12V clean?
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That photo settles it. The label reads **LRS-350-12**, INPUT 100-120V 6.8A or 200-240V 3.4A, OUTPUT 12V 29A, and I can now read the silkscreen next to each screw: **L, N, ⏚, -V, -V, +V, +V**.

Matching that against your wires: brown on L, blue on N, green/yellow on earth, the two black wires on the two -V screws, the two red wires on the two +V screws. Correct, polarity included. Nice work.

Worth knowing: an LRS-350 run on 120V does not give the full 350W, it derates. Even so you are well clear, since the Thor P2 only wants about 166W.

So go ahead with the power-up test from my last message:
1. Mains in, nothing on the XT60. Listen for anything odd.
2. Meter in the XT60 socket: roughly 12.0 to 12.3V, red pin positive.
3. Mains out, XT60 onto the miner, mains back in.

And that black tape over the terminals is a stopgap, not a cover. A proper terminal shield or a box is worth the few dollars.
It is covered, no way to touch any terminals, got it from you guys.

Understood, that is settled then. I was only going by what the photo showed.

You are good to go: mains in with nothing on the XT60, check it sits quiet, then mains out, XT60 onto the Thor P2, mains back in.

If anything looks off once it boots, chip temps, hashrate, a code on the screen, come back and tell me what it shows.
ok, thanks.
You are welcome. Good luck with it, and enjoy the quiet.
